idea.description: Test bounded moderate-negative replacement within each category’s single BERT4Rec, retaining separately normalized recent-terminal and ordinary Cloze supervision. Replace 16 of 64 uniform negatives with descending ranks 9–24 from an 80-item uniform remainder scored by the current network. This corrects the previous ranks 33–80 rule, which favored easier negatives. The proposal is a controlled experiment, not a measured improvement or an executable replacement for the unavailable corrected baseline.
idea.motivation: The retained recent-terminal component targets revival of older isolated interests; competitive candidate training targets broadly related items outranking direct recent-interest matches. These mechanisms address two diagnosed user-facing failures as hypotheses, without identifying fulfilled needs, ownership or exact compatibility. Electronics’ 6.62% sampled ranking-error rate and 0.7269 lower-tail margin motivate the model-facing discrimination hypothesis, while remaining distinct from validation HR@10. At early research progress, a sampler change remains more feasible than adding text encoders or temporal attention. Its incremental benefit is uncertain because candidate cross-entropy already assigns larger gradients to higher-scoring negatives.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected BERT4Rec, all four categories and existing routing. Train exactly one independent network per category within each experimental condition; compare conditions without combining their predictions. Deploy only one selected checkpoint per category. No checkpoint averaging, independent experts, auxiliary fitted popularity/transition scores or other score fusion is allowed.

Retain the fixed mixed objective in both conditions. For batch size B>=2, construct floor(B/2) terminal examples and the remaining ordinary baseline-Cloze examples. Sample eligible training users uniformly with replacement from users having at least two interactions. For history length n, terminal target t is sampled uniformly from indices n-min(10,n-1) through n-1, inclusive, using zero-based indexing. Construct history[max(0,t-(L-1)):t] followed by MASK and left-pad to L. Exclude the entire future suffix. Preserve the corrected baseline’s Cloze windowing and target-selection rules, recording their actual settings rather than inventing a mask rate. Every supervised target is replaced by the reserved MASK; no unchanged-target corruption is permitted. Ensure at least one supervised position per eligible Cloze example. Normalize terminal and Cloze losses separately over valid supervised positions and combine with weights 0.5 and 0.5. If only one component has valid targets, give it weight 1 and record the event; skip an update only when neither has valid targets.

Compare uniform-64 candidate cross-entropy against moderate-negative replacement, holding architecture, initialization, optimizer, batch size, terminal/Cloze examples, temperature 1.0 and all unrelated settings fixed. A historical measurement is a valid control only if its configuration and checkpoint eligibility actually match. The supplied 0.5737 inspiration score does not establish performance for either the corrected sampler or an otherwise unmatched control. If no matching control exists, include its training in the experiment budget.

For each target, eligible negatives are real catalog IDs excluding PAD, MASK and every item in that user’s complete training history, which includes the supervised positive. Never consult validation or test labels for exclusions. Sample P=min(128,eligible_count) unique items uniformly without replacement. Use bounded rejection with exact-complement fallback, or exact complement sampling; never use an unbounded rejection loop. When P=128, reserve 48 uniformly selected IDs. Sort the remaining 80 by detached current-model score descending, breaking ties by ascending item ID, and select ranks 9–24 inclusive. Combine those 16 with the reserved 48. For 65<=P<128, use 64 uniformly selected candidates; for P<=64, use all P. Skip targets with P=0 and record counts. Mask unused candidate slots to negative infinity during batching.

The corrected rank window has mean descending rank 16.5 within the remainder, compared with 40.5 for a uniform remainder item; the previous ranks 33–80 had mean rank 56.5 and therefore favored easier negatives. These are order-statistic statements about score rank, not evidence of HR@10 gains or negative-label reliability. Skipping the top eight is only a false-negative-risk heuristic. The 48 uniform items may still include very high-scoring candidates. Do not call selected items confirmed negatives or claim that this rule inherits Hard-BPR’s robustness.

Match candidate pools between conditions at matching update and supervised-position indices. Generate a shared random permutation of the pool: both conditions use its first 48 as the uniform component; the control uses the next 16, while mining chooses ranks 9–24 from the remaining 80. This gives the control a uniform subset of 64 and isolates selection conditional on the same pool. Refresh mining every optimizer batch using current parameters; do not add a separate fitted mining model or cache across updates. Candidate cross-entropy is an uncorrected sampled classification objective. Adaptive selection changes that objective and is not an unbiased approximation to full softmax.

For mining, save was_training=model.training, call model.eval(), and recompute encoder features from the exact masked inputs inside torch.no_grad(). Merely detaching features previously computed with dropout active does not implement dropout-free mining. Score candidate chunks and maintain a running top-24 ordered by score and item ID; ranks 9–24 can then be recovered without retaining all scoring intermediates. Restore model.train(was_training) in a finally block. During optimization explicitly ensure training mode, recompute features with gradients enabled and rescore selected IDs through the actual trained item embeddings. Detached mining features or scores must never substitute for differentiable optimization scores. Full target IDs and target text, if any, remain hidden at supervised positions.

Use memory-safe input microbatches. Determine valid target counts N_terminal and N_cloze before backward, zero gradients once, and independently recompute each microbatch’s training features. Backward its weighted loss sum immediately, divided by the original full-batch component denominator; step once after all microbatches. Do not average unequal chunk means or retain all differentiable chunk graphs by summing them before backward. Keep each target’s complete positive-plus-negatives candidate axis together for cross-entropy. Splitting that axis requires an exact global log-sum-exp normalizer, not independent chunk softmaxes. Keep microbatch size, ordering and loss weights identical across conditions.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Use explicit independent streams for initialization, training-user/example selection, masking, dropout, candidate-pool generation and uniform reservation. Seed each deterministically from 42 and record the derivation, RNG implementation and states; never let mining consume example or dropout RNG draws. Match initial parameters category by category across conditions, without loading checkpoints from another trial. Record reproducibility limitations of GPU kernels and avoid claiming bitwise identity unless verified.

Before execution, record the remaining shared GPU-second allowance and allocate half to each condition, equally divided among its four categories, including training, mining, validation, diagnostics and failures. Reserve time for mandatory diagnostics inside each allocation using the host’s available timing information; do not invent a runtime estimate. Do not silently reallocate a failed run’s allowance or add tuning trials. Stop at completed epochs within each cap, respecting the 200-epoch ceiling, and record actual updates, masked-target counts, elapsed GPU seconds and stopping reasons. Mining adds an evaluation encoder forward and candidate scoring to the ordinary training forward/backward; measure its runtime rather than estimating speed from forward counts alone. Equal-time endpoints measure efficiency; common-update checkpoints measure sampling effects per update.

Predeclare validation after epochs 10,20,...,200, subject to the per-run caps. A paired macro checkpoint at epoch e is eligible only if all four categories in both conditions completed that epoch and the unchanged host protocol can score their four-checkpoint bundles. Compare methods on this common eligible grid, breaking ties within each condition toward the earlier epoch and ties between conditions toward the uniform control. Select the winning condition by its best macro validation HR@10 on that shared grid and deploy its corresponding four category checkpoints. Do not independently choose category epochs or combine conditions. Report scores at each common fixed-update checkpoint and the last eligible common checkpoint, alongside compute-limited endpoints when the host supplies those scores. Endpoint evaluations outside the common grid are descriptive and ineligible for selection. If no paired grid point is completed, report that the comparison is incomplete; do not manufacture a selection result or expand the budget. Use only host-exposed validation capabilities and the pinned evaluator; do not implement an alternate evaluator.

Retain identical pinned validation users and candidate sets. If the host supplies paired per-user hits, report category hit-rate differences, discordant hit counts and delta_macro=one quarter of the sum of category mean paired hit differences. Bootstrap paired user records with replacement independently within each category for 10,000 replicates using a recorded seed of 42, and report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and candidate sets, exclude training-seed variability and do not correct adaptive checkpoint selection. Without hit indicators, report aggregate scores without invented uncertainty. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Treat validation gains as exploratory; sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog superiority.

Track mining behavior using fixed diagnostic examples and candidate pools: selected-negative score ranks, positive-minus-selected-negative margins, fallback frequency and eligible-pool sizes. If measured, also summarize selected-item training-frequency distributions to detect popularity concentration. These are descriptive checks, not additional selection objectives. Preserve the original uniform-negative diagnostic stream so changing optimization sampling does not mechanically change existing margin metrics. Raw margins remain score-scale dependent. Do not reinterpret directional similarity as recommendation diversity or single-negative margins as validation HR@10. Recent-target sampling may overweight transient or popular interests; mining may amplify plausible unseen positives, popularity shortcuts and memorization. Excluding known positives does not resolve these risks. Avoid further rank-window tuning on the same validation users within this proposal; record every attempted configuration.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView and the actual nn.Module at view.model. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), using the measured metrics and definitions. Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), B x L, with family-correct MASK-position supervision. Preserve metric definitions and report unavailable metadata explicitly. Only public interaction histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are available; reviews, ratings, item categories, ownership, prices, stores and simulator traits must not be invented.

Inference retains at most L-1 history items, appends MASK, left-pads and gathers the final nonpadding position using explicit position indices, never count-1. Exclude PAD and MASK from recommendation outputs. Architecture is unchanged, but verify that the predictor writer emits matching model configuration and state-dict loading, and each category loads exactly one checkpoint. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for the twenty simulator users as qualitative diagnosis, not another selection metric. Do not fetch extra data or pretrained weights, inspect other trials, reuse their checkpoints, read hidden test files or change the host evaluator.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare two conditions: uniform64 and moderate_replacement.
Record shared budget allocations, RNG streams, common checkpoint grid and tie rules.
For each condition and category:
    Initialize the corrected single BERT4Rec with matched seed-42 parameters.
    For each completed epoch, execute exactly 200 batches:
        Construct identical terminal/Cloze examples at matching update indices.
        Replace every supervised target with MASK; omit terminal future suffixes.
        For each supervised position belonging to user u:
            eligible = real_catalog - {PAD, MASK} - set(training_history[u])
            pool = shared_uniform_unique_pool(eligible, min(128, len(eligible)))
            order = shared_random_permutation(pool)
            If len(pool) == 128:
                uniform48 = order[:48]
                remainder80 = order[48:]
                If condition == uniform64:
                    negatives = uniform48 + remainder80[:16]
                Else:
                    defer selection of 16 IDs to mining
            Else:
                negatives = order[:min(64, len(order))]
            Record and exclude targets having no eligible negatives.
        Determine full-batch valid terminal and Cloze denominators.
        Set component weights to (0.5,0.5), or 1 for the sole valid component.
        If moderate_replacement has targets requiring mining:
            was_training = model.training
            try:
                model.eval()
                with torch.no_grad():
                    For each input microbatch requiring mining:
                        features = model.log2feats(the_same_masked_sequences)
                        For each qualifying target:
                            Score remainder80 in chunks.
                            Maintain top24 by descending score, ascending item-ID ties.
                            negatives = uniform48 + top24[8:24]
            finally:
                model.train(was_training)
        If no valid targets: record skipped update; continue.
        model.train()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        For each input microbatch in fixed order:
            features = model.log2feats(masked_sequences)  # gradients enabled
            logits = differentiable_scores(features, [positive] + selected_negatives)
            losses = per_target_cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0)
            weighted_sum = sum over components of:
                component_weight * microbatch_component_loss_sum / full_batch_component_count
            weighted_sum.backward()
        Apply unchanged baseline gradient clipping, if configured.
        optimizer.step()
    Save eligible trial-local checkpoints; invoke unchanged host validation when available.
    Charge mining, validation, diagnostics and failures to the allocated compute cap.
Compare macro HR@10 on epochs completed by all categories in both conditions.
Use the same eligible epoch grid; earlier-epoch ties and uniform-condition ties win.
Report common-update differences, measured runtime and descriptive time endpoints.
If available, bootstrap paired validation hits within categories, never training seeds.
Deploy the winning condition's same-epoch bundle: one checkpoint per category.
Emit matching appended-MASK inference; gather final nonpadding position explicitly.
Run preserved family-specific diagnostics with fixed uniform diagnostic negatives.

originality.positive: Provides a precise, reproducible adaptation of moderate-negative selection to inference-aligned masked BERT4Rec training.
originality.negative: Rank-window mining, random/hard mixtures and terminal masking are established mechanisms; the corrected window is a heuristic rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: A matched comparison can establish whether harder candidate competition warrants later temporal or text-aware investigation and quantify its compute cost.
future_potential.negative: Candidate cross-entropy already emphasizes high scores; incremental gains may be small, benchmark dependent or offset by false negatives and mining overhead.

code_difficulty.positive: Preserves the BERT4Rec architecture and inference path, concentrating functional changes in sampling and training execution.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct evaluation-mode mining, independent RNG streams, matched candidate pools, component-normalized microbatch backward and budget-matched checkpoint selection require substantial care.

idea_diagnosis.description: Test a predeclared endpoint-supervision weight of 0.75 against the corrected BERT4Rec baseline, retaining one independently trained model per category. Combine endpoint-only and ordinary reconstruction losses in one optimizer update while preserving each group’s original loss reduction. Treat this as a controlled supervision-allocation experiment, rather than a novel masking mechanism.
idea_diagnosis.motivation: Endpoint masking matches the absence of right context at appended-mask inference and is already established in BERT4Rec. The supplied diagnostic shows weaker training separation for Electronics, but does not demonstrate that context mismatch causes that weakness. A controlled weight change tests whether supervision allocation improves the common validation metric without changing the backbone or introducing independent predictors. Early research progress favors this small experiment over architectural expansion; the matched context-gap probe remains a useful budgeted diagnostic.
idea_diagnosis.implementation_notes:
First document the supplied baseline’s precise loss, reduction, group construction, masking policy, optimizer-step construction and endpoint frequency; these are not provided here. Do not substitute the original paper or released implementation for the corrected host baseline. The paper describes averaging masked-target negative log-likelihood within sequences, whereas the released implementation sums real masked-target losses across the batch and divides by their count plus 1e-5. The released generator ordinarily creates D=10 reconstruction copies plus one endpoint-only copy per window; ordinary copies may also mask endpoints. This 1/11 endpoint-example fraction does not establish endpoint loss weight, and overlapping-window construction must not be imported into the host baseline.

Classify groups by generation provenance, not by whether a sampled mask happens to occupy the final position. If the supplied baseline lacks these explicit groups, retain its exact control and add a matched-construction control before attributing differences to weighting. Predeclare this decision before training; reduce the experiment set if the required controls exceed budget. Ensure both groups are nonempty for each candidate update without silently modifying only the candidate’s sampling. Preserve baseline within-group reduction, including denominator constants; per-example normalization is a separately labeled ablation. For a global token mean, reproduce the exact baseline from group loss sums and counts rather than assuming equal group weights. Omit duplicate objectives, including alpha=0.75 if it already reproduces the control.

Use identical seeded prefix draws, group membership and corruption masks across comparison arms, with separate deterministic sampling and model-randomness streams. Keep total examples, realized supervised targets, optimizer steps and evaluation schedule matched across arms. Endpoint and reconstruction groups need not have equal target counts. Record their sizes, targets, terminal-target frequency, retained context length and actual GPU time. Predeclare equal maximum GPU-time allocations as budget caps; compare matched completed updates where feasible and disclose any unequal completion. The coefficient changes gradient allocation and potentially gradient variance, so a gain cannot independently identify context mismatch as its cause.

Endpoint inputs contain a training-prefix target replaced by reserved MASK, clean preceding context, and truncation reserving the target position. Every supervised input target must be MASK, with labels used only in the loss. Ordinary reconstruction retains the corrected baseline’s eligible positions, mask-count rule and nonempty-target policy; do not add endpoint fallback for empty masks. Never expose shifted targets through bidirectional inputs or silently replace the baseline loss with catalog cross-entropy.

Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Keep execution single-GPU. Charge all comparison training, diagnosis, validation and failures to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Each deployed category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint; no checkpoint averaging, independent experts or score fusion. Preserve predictor-writer consistency and appended-mask inference: retain at most N-1 observed items, append MASK, left-pad and read its final nonpadding position, never count-1.

They measure model dependence, not causal preference. Any effective-rank probe must specify embedding sample, centering, singular-value normalization and entropy convention.

Select solely using the unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. spec = document_corrected_baseline_objective_and_sampling()
plan = predeclare_exact_baseline_and_weight_candidate(alpha=0.75)
if explicit_group_construction_changes_baseline(spec):
    plan.require_matched_construction_control()
plan.omit_algebraically_duplicate_arms()
plan.allocate_shared_gpu_budget_including_controls_and_diagnostics()

for arm in plan.arms:
    for category in four_categories:
        model = initialize_corrected_bert4rec(seed=42)
        stream = reset_identical_seeded_sampling_stream(category)
        for epoch in range(at_most_200):
            for step in range(200):
                stop_if_predeclared_allocation_exhausted()
                batch = stream.draw_arm_appropriate_batch(arm)
                assert_supervised_inputs_are_reserved_MASK(batch)
                terms = compute_unchanged_baseline_loss_terms(model, batch)
                if arm == 'exact_baseline':
                    loss = spec.exact_reduce(terms)
                else:
                    E, R = partition_by_generation_provenance(terms)
                    if arm == 'matched_construction_control':
                        loss = spec.exact_reduce(concatenate(E, R))
                    else:
                        assert_nonempty_groups(E, R)
                        loss = 0.75 * spec.reduce_within_group(E) + 0.25 * spec.reduce_within_group(R)
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                record_counts_updates_context_and_gpu_time()
        save_one_category_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(model)

originality.negative: BERT4Rec already includes endpoint-only supervision, and fixed weighted objectives are established; 0.75 is a heuristic coefficient.

future_potential.negative: A small benchmark gain may reflect gradient allocation, popularity shortcuts or adaptive validation search rather than the proposed context-mismatch mechanism.

evolution_history.description: Train each category's single BERT4Rec with ordinary Cloze supervision plus a curriculum of recent terminal-prefix examples. Test whether replacing a modest fraction of uniform training negatives with reproducibly selected title-confusable candidates improves fixed macro validation HR@10.
evolution_history.motivation: Address two observed user failures: broadly plausible recommendations displacing specific choices, and historical interests outweighing recent priorities. Target negative lower-tail positive–negative margins in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics. These mechanisms are indirect: lexical similarity does not reveal compatibility or current intent, and larger training margins do not establish validation gains. Embedding scores near 0.5 provide no basis for a collapse-removal objective.
evolution_history.implementation_notes:
Architecture and data: retain the corrected host BERT4Rec backbone, reserved MASK, bidirectional masked-target learning, appended-mask inference, four-category routing, and one independently trained model/checkpoint per category. No independent predictors or inference fusion. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, supplied splits, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Use only public training interactions and permitted titles/descriptions/timestamps. Do not use unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, simulator traits, hidden test files, external datasets, pretrained weights, or other trials' checkpoints.

Terminal construction: sample users uniformly among training histories of length n>=2. Use one-indexed endpoints t in {2,...,n}. Define r_beta(t)=exp[-beta*(n-t)/(n-2)]/Z for n>2 and the sole endpoint t=2 for n=2. Use p(t)=0.5/(n-1)+0.5*r_beta(t), beta=2; beta=0 is the uniform control. The visible sequence contains the last L-1 interactions strictly before t, followed by MASK, then left padding. Target x_t never appears in its target position; all later interactions are absent. Earlier genuine repeats may remain. Let q(epoch)=0.25+0.25*min(epoch/50,1), with epochs numbered from zero. Sample one task branch per batch: terminal with probability q, otherwise unchanged baseline random Cloze. Never feed shifted targets through a bidirectional visible sequence.

Lexical index: fit per-category word TF–IDF using available titles only, Unicode NFKC normalization, case folding, whitespace collapse, sklearn word unigrams/bigrams, token_pattern='(?u)\\b\\w\\w+\\b', min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True, norm='l2'. This uses permitted catalog metadata, without interaction labels beyond training. Construct exact sparse cosine neighborhoods in bounded blocks; avoid a dense catalog-by-catalog matrix. Sort positive-similarity neighbors by descending cosine, then ascending item ID. Remove normalized-title duplicates and cosine>=0.95 candidates as a proposed, unvalidated safeguard. Define the moderate pool as original sorted ranks 11–50 after duplicate removal. Then remove the target and all items in that user's observed training history, and renormalize uniformly over remaining pool members. Missing/empty titles or empty pools trigger uniform fallback. These numerical choices are fixed initial hypotheses, not literature-established thresholds. Log pool coverage, fallback frequency, lexical similarity, and detached model-score difficulty separately.

Sampling and objective: for each terminal target draw K=32 unique eligible negatives, or all eligible items if fewer exist. In C draw H=min(8,floor(K_actual/4)) uniformly without replacement from the eligible lexical pool, reducing H when necessary; draw K_actual-H uniformly without replacement from remaining eligible real items. If H=0 use uniform-only loss. Otherwise L_terminal=(1-alpha)*mean(softplus(s_random-s_positive))+alpha*mean(softplus(s_lexical-s_positive)), alpha=H/K_actual<=0.25. Thus sampling counts and branch loss weights are explicit; the lexical branch contributes at most 25% of loss weight, but individual loss values or gradients are not capped. Uniform controls use the mean pairwise loss over the same total negative count. If no eligible negatives exist, resample the example with a bounded retry policy and record skips. Keep the ordinary Cloze loss unchanged and record its exact reduction from the supplied baseline. Expected mixed loss is (1-q)*L_Cloze+q*L_terminal; alternate-branch training estimates this directly. Pairwise loss does not approximate full softmax, and no uniform LogQ correction is applied to mined candidates. Excluding all known training-history positives affects sampling only; later interactions are never exposed as model inputs or targets. Future unobserved positives remain a false-negative risk.

Controlled search: predeclare at most four configurations: baseline Cloze; uniform-endpoint terminal mixture with uniform pairwise negatives; recency-endpoint terminal mixture with uniform pairwise negatives; the same recency mixture with lexical negatives. The first comparison jointly changes terminal exposure and its objective, so it cannot isolate masking from loss. The second isolates endpoint recency; the third isolates lexical sampling conditional on the pairwise setup. A separate CE control is desirable only if budget remains: use full-catalog CE over real items, excluding PAD/MASK, on identical sampled terminal targets. Never attribute CE-versus-pairwise differences to negative mining. Keep backbone, optimizer, negative count, seeds, and planned training steps matched wherever applicable. Fix validation checks every 10 epochs, select the earliest checkpoint on exact macro-HR ties, log every look and GPU cost, and cap total GPU consumption at 43,200 seconds. Before launch estimate a common epoch cap <=200 that permits the planned comparisons; if insufficient, prioritize baseline, uniform terminal control, and recency control before lexical mining. Interrupted or unmatched runs are exploratory rather than clean matched-compute comparisons. Use a predeclared practical threshold of +0.005 absolute macro HR@10 as a descriptive selection threshold, not a significance guarantee. If C does not clear it versus its immediate uniform-negative control, prefer the simpler control. All selection uses validation only.

Evaluation and shortcut checks: retain identical 200 validation users/category, the pinned 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42, masking, history truncation, and tie handling. When host outputs expose per-user hits, report gained/lost hits and macro delta; bootstrap paired users within category 10,000 times with analysis seed 42 and equal category weights for a 95% percentile interval. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain unavailable outputs. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidate sets; they exclude seed/candidate uncertainty and do not correct winner optimism. Exact per-category McNemar tests or macro paired randomization are optional exploratory analyses, not additional selection criteria. Inspect paired ranks, margins, history-length strata, and text-coverage strata when available. Do not optimize lexical-overlap diagnostics or treat unidentified-item skips as rejection. Title resemblance can promote lexical shortcuts; the uniform control and unchanged evaluator test utility, while full-catalog recommendations for twenty training users remain qualitative and cannot establish population or benchmark performance. Preserve untouched final evaluation for host confirmation.

Compatibility: retain ModelView, view.model as the actual nn.Module, view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Adapt probes to genuinely masked target positions, never shifted visible targets. Freeze diagnostic samples, negative IDs, padding, masking, and tie rules across comparisons. Mark missing metadata attribution as unavailable. Read each left-padded sequence using max occupied position; appended MASK is normally at L-1. Serialize architecture configuration, reserved token IDs, item mapping, weights, and any required inference state through the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs exactly the selected single model. Lexical pools are training-only. No host baseline source is included in this prompt, so the algorithm below is reproducible pseudocode rather than a claimed drop-in train.py.
evolution_history.pseudocode:
predeclare configurations, validation cadence, compute cap, tie rule, and selection threshold
for configuration in budget_feasible_predeclared_order:
    for category in four_categories:
        seed_training(42)
        model = initialize_corrected_host_BERT4Rec()
        lexical_pools = build_deterministic_title_TFIDF_pools_if_required()
        for epoch in range(common_epoch_cap_at_most_200):
            q = 0.25 + 0.25 * min(epoch / 50, 1)
            for batch_index in range(200):
                if configuration_uses_terminal and Bernoulli(q):
                    user = sample_uniform_eligible_training_user()
                    history = training_history(user)
                    t = sample_endpoint(history, beta=configuration_beta,
                                        uniform_mixture_weight=0.5)
                    target = history[t - 1]
                    preceding = history[:t - 1]
                    sequence = left_pad(preceding[-(L - 1):] + [MASK], L)
                    eligible = real_items_excluding(target, all_training_items(user))
                    negatives, branch_labels = sample_unique_negatives(
                        eligible, K=32, lexical_limit=8,
                        lexical_pool=lexical_pools[target] if enabled else None)
                    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                    mask_position = max_index_where(sequence != PAD)
                    positive_score = model.predict_score(features[mask_position], target)
                    negative_scores = model.predict_score(features[mask_position], negatives)
                    loss = normalized_pairwise_branch_loss(
                        positive_score, negative_scores, branch_labels,
                        lexical_weight=lexical_count / total_negative_count)

def _uniform_pool(interacted, itemnum, count, rng):

    selected, seen = [], set()

        terminal = row < terminal_count

            supervised = [(maxlen - 1, history[t])]
        else:
            items = history[-maxlen:]
            seq[-len(items) :] = items

        np.asarray(columns, dtype=np.int64),

def _select_negatives(model, sequence, rows, columns, pools, mine):

def backward_objective_batch(model, batch, device):
    sequence, rows, columns, targets, pools, groups, mine, excluded, fallback = batch

    if not len(rows):
        return None, counts, excluded, fallback

    total = 0.0

            logits,
            torch.zeros(len(hidden), dtype=torch.long, device=hidden.device),
            reduction="none",
        )

    # Parameters remain fixed until all microbatches have contributed gradients.
    for start in range(0, len(sequence), INPUT_MICROBATCH):
        stop = min(start + INPUT_MICROBATCH, len(sequence))
        keep = (rows >= start) & (rows < stop)
        if not keep.any():
            continue
        seq_t = torch.as_tensor(sequence[start:stop], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        row_t = torch.as_tensor(rows[keep] - start, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        col_t = torch.as_tensor(columns[keep], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        pool_t = torch.as_tensor(pools[keep], dtype=torch.long, device=device)

        candidates = torch.cat((positive[:, None], negatives), dim=1)
        weights = np.asarray(
            [1.0 / (active_components * counts[int(group)]) for group in groups[keep]],
            dtype=np.float32,
        )
        weight_t = torch.as_tensor(weights, device=device)
        model.train()
        hidden = model.log2feats(seq_t)[row_t, col_t]
        terms = []
        for offset in range(0, len(hidden), 256):

                hidden[offset : offset + 256],
                candidates[offset : offset + 256],

                preserve_rng_state=False,

    return total, counts, excluded, fallback
